debate_title: Do AI benchmark scores predict real-world usefulness?

conflicts.point: Whether pre-deployment safety gates or decentralized commercial deployment loops are more effective at mitigating structural AI failures.

positions.stance: Mandatory pre-deployment safety gates are required to prevent systemic operational failures because market feedback is a lagging indicator of harm.
Decentralized commercial deployment loops and rapid patching fix metric saturation and model vulnerabilities much faster than pre-emptive regulatory compliance gates.

verdicts.conflict: Whether pre-deployment safety gates or decentralized commercial deployment loops are more effective at mitigating structural AI failures.
verdicts.rationale: The safetyist position correctly identifies that high-stakes domains require upstream verification, but relies on an aviation analogy that ignores the rapid update cycles of digital software. Conversely, the accelerationist position champions fast market feedback but discounts catastrophic tail risks in domains like healthcare and legal compliance. Neither camp provides sufficient empirical data to prove that one governance mechanism scales better across all risk tiers.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Longitudinal incident tracking data from sectors utilizing both regulatory models would clarify whether pre-market gates or continuous patching better prevent systemic harms.
